name: Noun–adjective gender agreement
rule: A feminine noun (usually ending ة) takes a feminine adjective, which adds ة.

name: Present-tense verb prefixes (he / she / they)
rule: The present-tense verb prefix changes with the subject: يَـ (he), تَـ (she), يَـ…ونَ (they).

name: Sun & moon letters (definite-article assimilation)
rule: ال is pronounced before moon letters; before the 14 sun letters ل is silent and the consonant doubles.

name: Singular, dual & plural nouns
rule: An Arabic noun is singular (بَيْتٌ), dual, or plural. The dual is regular — add ـَانِ to any noun: كِتَابٌ ← كِتَابَانِ (two books). Plurals are either sound — masculine ـُونَ (مُعَلِّمُونَ), feminine ـَاتٌ (طَاوِلَاتٌ) — or broken, an internal reshaping learned with each word: كِتَابٌ ← كُتُبٌ. A plural of non-human things is treated as feminine singular for agreement: كُتُبٌ جَمِيلَةٌ.
commonErrors: Giving a non-human plural a plural adjective: كُتُبٌ كِبَارٌ instead of كُتُبٌ كَبِيرَةٌ.
Expecting one plural ending for every noun — broken plurals vary and are learned individually.

name: Definite & indefinite (ال and tanwīn)
rule: A noun is indefinite or definite. Indefinite nouns end in tanwīn — a doubled final vowel, usually ـٌ ("-un"): كِتَابٌ (a book). Definite nouns take the prefix الـ and lose the tanwīn: الْكِتَابُ (the book). الـ and tanwīn never appear on the same word.
commonErrors: Writing الـ and tanwīn together: الْكِتَابٌ.
Dropping the tanwīn from an indefinite noun — بَاب on its own should be بَابٌ.

name: The nominal sentence (no verb "to be")
rule: A nominal sentence has no verb. It puts a definite topic (mubtadaʾ) next to an indefinite comment (khabar): الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ = "the-house big" = "The house is big." Arabic has no present-tense word for "is" or "are". The khabar agrees with the topic in gender.
commonErrors: Looking for a word that means "is" — there is none.
Making the khabar definite: الْبَيْتُ الْكَبِيرُ means "the big house", not a sentence.

name: Demonstratives (هَذَا / هَذِهِ / هَؤُلَاءِ)
rule: هَذَا (this, m.), هَذِهِ (this, f.) and هَؤُلَاءِ (these, pl.) point at something and agree with its gender. Before an indefinite noun they form a sentence: هَذَا كِتَابٌ (this is a book). Before a definite noun they mean "this …": هَذَا الْكِتَابُ (this book).
commonErrors: Using هَذَا with a feminine noun: هَذَا بِنْتٌ should be هَذِهِ بِنْتٌ.
Reading هَذَا الْكِتَابُ as a full sentence — with the definite noun it is just "this book".

name: Attached possessive pronouns (ـِي ـكَ ـهُ ـهَا)
rule: Possession is shown by a suffix on the noun, not a separate word: ـِي (my), ـكَ (your, m.), ـكِ (your, f.), ـهُ (his), ـهَا (her). A noun with a possessive suffix is already definite, so it takes no الـ and no tanwīn: كِتَابِي (my book), بَيْتُهُ (his house).
commonErrors: Adding الـ to a possessed noun: الْكِتَابِي.
Keeping the tanwīn before the suffix: كِتَابٌي.

name: Core prepositions (فِي عَلَى مِنْ إِلَى مَعَ بِـ لِـ)
rule: The common prepositions are فِي (in), عَلَى (on), مِنْ (from), إِلَى (to), مَعَ (with), and the prefixes بِـ (with / by) and لِـ (for / to). The noun after a preposition is in the genitive — with الـ it ends ـِ (فِي الْبَيْتِ), indefinite it ends ـٍ (فِي بَيْتٍ).
commonErrors: Leaving a gap after بِـ or لِـ — they attach directly: بِالْقَلَمِ, not بِ الْقَلَمِ.
Using the ـُ ending after a preposition: فِي الْبَيْتُ should be فِي الْبَيْتِ.

name: Negating the nominal sentence (لَيْسَ / لَا / مَا)
rule: To negate a nominal sentence use لَيْسَ (is / are not) before the comment: لَيْسَ الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرًا (the house is not big) — the comment takes ـً after لَيْسَ. لَا negates the noun that follows it ("no …", "there is no …"); مَا is a plainer "not" before the comment.
commonErrors: Using لَا where لَيْسَ is needed — لَا الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ is not a sentence.
Forgetting the ـً on the comment after لَيْسَ: لَيْسَ الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ.
